'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[November 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
****The [[Taliban]] kill at least 12 [[Afghan National Police|police]] officers and injure 10 others in [[Jurm District]], [[Badakhshan Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-167822 (TOLOnews)]
***[[Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan#Plans_by_the_administration_of_Donald_Trump|Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan]]
****[[The Pentagon]] announces a partial withdrawal of 2,000 more [[U.S. troop]]s from [[Afghanistan]] by mid-January. The withdrawal will reduce the number of U.S. [[military personnel]] stationed in Afghanistan from 4,500 to 2,500. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-trump/trump-to-cut-troop-levels-in-afghanistan-but-stops-short-of-full-withdrawal-idUSKBN27X2PE (Reuters)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**The [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey]] approves [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]]'s request to deploy [[Turkish Land Forces|Turkish Army]] peacekeepers to monitor a [[2020 Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire agreement|ceasefire agreement]] between [[Armenia]] and [[Azerbaijan]] in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201117-nagorno-karabakh-turkey-to-send-peacekeepers-to-azerbaijan-to-monitor-truce (France 24)]
**[[Armenia]] and [[Azerbaijan]] exchange the bodies of at least 200 people killed in clashes in Nagorno-Karabakh. The exchange was overseen by [[Russia]]n peacekeepers, according to the [[Red Cross]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/17/armenia-azerbaijan-exchange-troops-bodies-as-part-of-peace-deal (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**[[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Ethiopian Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] vows a "final and crucial" offensive after a three-day deadline to the leaders of the [[Tigray Region]] to surrender has expired. Abiy also confirms that [[airstrike]]s are being carried out but defines them as "precision-led and surgical", denying claims of civilian casualties. [https://apnews.com/article/international-news-eritrea-sudan-ethiopia-abiy-ahmed-46ca7257fa8ac7ee91a52f05bfda59d2 (AP)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**The bodies of 29 people are found in the [[Virunga National Park]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] after they were "executed en masse". The interior ministry of [[North Kivu]] [[provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|province]] has blamed the [[Allied Democratic Forces]] (ADF) and added that six other civilians were killed in a nearby village on Tuesday. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/17/dozens-killed-in-eastern-dr-congo-adf-militia-blamed (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
***[[Economy of Japan|Japanese economy]] grew at annualized rate of 21.4% in July-September quarter after two consecutive quarters of contraction due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]], driven by rise of private spending and exports. [https://apnews.com/article/business-tokyo-coronavirus-pandemic-japan-economy-e580d322d39c91454129394851245e19 (AP)]
*[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces a ban on the sale of new [[Petrol engine|petrol]] and [[diesel engine]] cars by 2030, as part of a [[government of the United Kingdom|government]] plan to reach a net zero emissions climate target in the [[United Kingdom]] by 2050. The sale of [[hybrid vehicle]]s will also be banned by 2035. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-climate-change-britain/britain-to-ban-new-petrol-cars-and-vans-by-2030-on-road-to-net-zero-emissions-idUSKBN27X2Z0 (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Idaho]]
*****[[Idaho]] reports 1,781 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single day record. [https://localnews8.com/health/coronavirus/2020/11/17/record-1781-new-idaho-covid-19-cases-35-new-deaths/ (KIFI-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Chuck Grassley]] of [[Iowa]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/17/politics/chuck-grassley-covid-19-senate-congress/index.html (CNN)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]]
*****[[New Mexico]] reports a record 2,112 new cases, bringing the statewide total to 67,559 cases. [https://www.sfreporter.com/news/2020/11/17/new-mexico-reports-record-daily-new-cases-of-2112/ (''Santa Fe Reporter'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
*****[[Pennsylvania Department of Health|Health Secretary]] [[Rachel Levine]] announces that out-of-state travelers will be required to either quarantine or present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] to enter the [[Pennsylvania|state]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pennsylvania-covid-restrictions-rachel-levine-watch-live-stream-today-2020-11-17/ (CBS News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
*****[[Ohio]] [[Governor of Ohio|Governor]] [[Mike DeWine]] orders a night time curfew from 10:00 p.m. until 5:00 a.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]] in an attempt to slow the spread of COVID-19. The curfew will begin on November 19 and will last for three weeks. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2020/11/17/ohio-governor-announces-10-pm-to-5-am-curfew-to-slow-spread-of-covid-19/ (WDIV-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
*****[[Wisconsin]] reports a record 92 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the death toll to 2,741. In addition, a record 318 hospitalizations are also reported. [https://www.wbay.com/2020/11/17/wisconsin-shatters-records-for-covid-19-deaths-hospitalizations/ (WBAY-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]]
*****[[Maine]] reports 246 new cases of COVID-19, a new single-day record. [https://wgme.com/news/local/maine-sets-another-single-day-record-with-246-new-coronavirus-cases-1-additional-death (WGME-TV)]
****[[Pfizer]] announces that they have launched a pilot delivery program for their potential vaccine in [[Rhode Island]], [[Texas]], [[New Mexico]], and [[Tennessee]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/526282-pfizer-launching-pilot-vaccine-delivery-program-in-four-states (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] reports a record 717 new cases and 11 deaths in the last 24 hours, bringing the provincial death toll to 310 and the total number of cases to 23,661. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/covid-19-bc-update-nov-17-1.5805802 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[First Minister of Scotland|First Minister]] [[Nicola Sturgeon]] announces that 11 local authorities, including [[Glasgow]], are to be placed into the highest level of restrictions (Level 4) for three weeks beginning at 6:00 p.m. [[Greenwich Mean Time|GMT]] on November 20. The Level 4 status for the 11 areas will remain in effect "for a limited time". [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-eleven-local-authorities-placed-into-scotlands-highest-level-of-restrictions-12134736 (Sky News)]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 598 new fatalities, the highest single-day total since May. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-britain-cases/uk-reports-highest-daily-covid-death-toll-since-may-idUSKBN27X2SZ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Cluster 5]]
*****The [[Government of Denmark|Minority government]] of [[Denmark]], held by [[Social Democrats (Denmark)|Social Democrats]], agrees with four left-leaning and center parties to support a law proposal that would allow for the culling of 15 million [[mink]]s across the country over concerns about a mutated version of the virus that has spread among the animals. The proposed law also bans [[mink farming]] until the end of next year. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/danish-government-gets-majority-to-back-plan-to-cull-minks/2020/11/17/a70e4220-28b9-11eb-9c21-3cc501d0981f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 442 new fatalities and 22,055 recoveries over the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 33,931 and nationwide recoveries to 1.47 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-sees-new-record-in-covid-19-deaths-recoveries/2046463 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****The number of total confirmed cases in [[Bulgaria]] surpasses 100,000, as the country sets a new record for daily deaths, with 152 fatalities reported in the last 24 hours. [https://coronavirus.bg/ (Coronavirus.bg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reported 45,422 new cases in the last 24 hours, surpassing two million total confirmed COVID-19 cases. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20201117-france-tops-2-million-covid-19-cases (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports 731 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since April 3, bringing the nationwide death toll to 46,464. [https://www.corriere.it/salute/20_novembre_17/coronavirus-italia-bollettino-oggi-17-novembre-32191-nuovi-casi-731-morti-d948bf94-28e2-11eb-92be-ccd547aa4d2b.shtml (''Corriere della Sera'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] reports 435 new fatalities, the highest daily increase in the second wave of the pandemic, bringing the death toll in the country to 41,688. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/spain-reports-435-new-covid-19-deaths--new-infections-slow-down-13580648 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces the closure of schools for the remainder of the semester and introduces a nationwide weekend curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 a.m. local time. Restrictions for senior citizens over 65 years of age will also be expanded to include people under 20 years of age, allowing them to go outside only from 10:00 a.m  to 4:00 p.m.. The new restrictions also order the closure of coffeehouses and cinemas, and for all sports events to be held without fans. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-introduces-partial-curfew-shuts-schools-amid-rising-covid-19-cases/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 13,352 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 788,473 cases. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1764366/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]]
****[[Jordan]] reports a record 6,454 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 155,993 cases. [https://en.royanews.tv/news/23554/2020-11-17 (Roya News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The [[Government of South Korea|government]] will increase [[social distancing]] rules in the [[Seoul Capital Area]] to Level 1.5 amidst a surge in COVID-19 cases. The new protocols will be enforced for [[Seoul]] and [[Gyeonggi Province]] beginning November 19, as well as in [[Incheon]] beginning November 23. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20201117003154320 (Yonhap News Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia)|Minister of State for Foreign Affairs]] of [[Saudi Arabia]] [[Adel al-Jubeir]] says that his country "reserves the right to arm itself with [[nuclear weapon]]s if [[Iran]] cannot be stopped from making one." [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/17/saudi-minister-wont-rule-out-nuclear-armament-over-iran (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Belarus–European Union relations]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Belarus]] opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] calls on [[Europe|European]] leaders to impose sanctions on supporters of [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] after police used tear gas, rubber bullets and stun grenades to disperse protesters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election-tsikhanouskaya/belarus-opposition-leader-calls-for-sanctions-on-lukashenko-supporters-idUSKBN27X1OZ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**[[Presidential transition of Joe Biden]]
***[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] and [[Vice President–elect of the United States|Vice President-elect]] [[Kamala Harris]] attend an unofficial security briefing from a team consisting of former advisers to both the [[Presidency of Barack Obama|Obama]] and [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump]] administrations. The briefing stems from the Trump administration's refusal to cooperate with the Biden-Harris transition team. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-election/biden-kamala-harris-briefing-trump-transition-b1724404.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] fires [[Chris Krebs]], the [[Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency|Director]] of the [[Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency]] (CISA), which oversaw the security of the 2020 election. Deputy Director [[Matthew Travis]], who had expected to become acting director, is forced to resign. Krebs and the CISA have refuted Trump's accusations of voter fraud, calling the election the "most secure in American history". Trump has called Krebs' statements "highly inaccurate". [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/trump-fires-dhs-election-official/2020/11/17/97d3fa5c-251c-11eb-952e-0c475972cfc0_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Apple Inc.]] releases the first Mac computers with Apple Silicon M-series ARM64 processors including the MacBook Air, MacBook Pro 13-inch, and Mac Mini with M1 chip which marks a major performance boost over x86 Intel equipped Macs.[https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2020/11/apple-unleashes-m1/]
*[[Censorship of Facebook]]
**The [[Solomon Islands]] [[Cabinet of Solomon Islands|Cabinet]] passes a ban on the use of [[social media]] platform [[Facebook]] in the country, citing public misuse of the platform, and a need for stricter [[cybercrime]] legislation and regulation. Communications Minister [[Peter Shannel Agovaka]] says the ban does not require [[Parliament of the Solomon Islands|parliament]]'s approval, and will be enforced once operators "establish a [[Firewall (computing)|firewall]]" to block Facebook. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/430811/solomon-islands-to-ban-facebook (RNZ)]
